business_problem: Quarks needed to personalize social-discovery experiences and scale safety moderation for millions of users without the idle GPU costs, operational friction, and inflexibility it hit while trying to run open-weight models for unpredictable traffic.
solution_summary: Quarks standardized its AI stack on Gemini models and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform so it could serve personalization, safety, and image-enhancement use cases from one production foundation. The company first evaluated Gemma models on dedicated GPU resources, but fluctuating day-and-night request patterns left expensive capacity idle and made scaling difficult. By moving to Gemini and Agent Platform, Quarks can swap models in seconds, keep customer-facing assistants responsive, and run moderation pipelines without rebuilding infrastructure. Gemini powers context-aware guidance in products such as Affemity, optional profile-photo enhancement, and large-scale content moderation workflows. The platform lets Quarks reserve human review for nuanced edge cases while using Google Cloud-managed AI infrastructure to increase coverage, respond faster to incidents, and sustain multimodal experiences at global consumer scale.

data_flow: User profile data, prompts, and content enter Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, which invokes Gemini models for recommendation guidance, profile-photo enhancement, and moderation. Outputs either return directly to the user experience or escalate to human moderators when a case needs nuanced review.
business_outcome: Quarks improved personalization and platform safety at the same time, expanding moderation coverage to the entire service, cutting incident response to under a minute, and avoiding the GPU inefficiency that previously limited scale.
